conditions, auditability, and the GA bar.\\n\\n## Problem statement\\nCustomers operating production LLM workloads need a safe and auditable path to change model versions and serving configs (quantization, prompt templates, tool/function calling settings, safety filters, etc.). Today, most customers rely on ad-hoc approaches:\\n- \\u201cBig bang\\u201d route updates with manual rollback when issues occur.\\n- Parallel routes and client-side traffic splitting.\\n- Custom scripts to change model versions during low-traffic windows.\\n\\nThese approaches increase the risk of outages and quality regressions, slow down iteration, and reduce confidence in deploying improvements.\\n\\n### Why now\\n- We already have primitives (model versioning, routing policies, observability) but lack a cohesive, GA-ready workflow with guardrails and rollback.\\n- Enterprise prospects and regulated customers are explicitly asking for: approvals, audit logs, and change control evidence.\\n\\n## Goals (GA scope)\\n1. Provide a Console workflow to create, run, pause, and rollback canary rollouts on *Hosted routes*.\\n2. Provide policy guardrails to ensure safe rollouts: max step size, minimum soak time, approval gates, and automatic stop/rollback on SLO breaches.\\n3. Provide customer-visible transparency: rollout timeline + cohort metric comparisons (baseline vs canary).\\n4. Emit complete audit logs for rollout actions.\\n5. Ensure the implementation is reliable, observable, and operable by on-call.\\n\\n## Non-goals (explicitly out of GA scope)\\n- Multi-armed bandits or automatic traffic optimization.\\n- Fully automated quality-eval gating as a hard requirement (quality metrics may be displayed or optionally provided as manual inputs).\\n- GA parity for Dedicated/Private workflows (schema compatibility is required, but Hosted is the GA target).\\n\\n## Target users / personas\\n- **ML Engineer / Platform Engineer (primary):** needs safe rollout tooling, metrics comparisons, quick rollback.\\n- **SRE / Reliability Engineer (secondary):** needs SLO-based auto-stop, low-noise alerting, clear runbooks.\\n- **Security / Compliance (secondary):** needs audit logs, approvals, role-based permissions, retention/export posture.\\n\\n## User stories\\n### Create and run a canary rollout\\n1. As a user, I can select a Hosted route and choose a baseline and canary model version/config.\\n2. As a user, I can define a traffic schedule (step list) and see validation/warnings if it violates policy.\\n3. As a user, I can start a rollout and watch baseline vs canary metrics and the rollout timeline.\\n\\n### Safety and change control\\n4. As an org admin, I can enforce guardrails (max % step, min soak time, approvals required) per tenant/tier.\\n5. As a rollout operator, I can pause a rollout and resume later.\\n6. As a rollout operator, I can rollback immediately to 0% canary (100% baseline) and lock the rollout to prevent accidental re-advance.\\n7. As a compliance reviewer, I can see an audit trail of who did what, when, and what changed.\\n\\n### Automatic protection\\n8. As a customer, I can configure (or accept defaults for) stop conditions so that a rollout pauses or rolls back on error/latency regressions.\\n9. As Redwood SRE, I can trust that stop conditions do not produce alert storms and that we have enough telemetry to diagnose false positives.\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Hosted route:** Customer-facing API endpoint in Redwood Hosted (e.g., `/v1/chat/completions` route mapped to a model/version/config).\\n- **Baseline:** The currently serving model/version/config for the route.\\n- **Canary:** The candidate model/version/config introduced during rollout.\\n- **Cohort:** Baseline vs canary traffic buckets used for metric comparisons.\\n- **Step:** Target canary traffic percentage for a time window (soak).\\n\\n## Requirements\\n### Functional requirements (GA)\\n#### Console workflow\\n- Provide a wizard-like flow:\\n  1) Select route\\n  2) Choose baseline and canary (model version + config)\\n  3) Configure schedule (steps + soak times)\\n  4) Configure guardrails / stop conditions (as allowed)\\n  5) Review + confirm\\n- Provide a rollout detail page with:\\n  - Current state (Draft/Running/Paused/Completed/Rolled back/Failed)\\n  - Current step target and time remaining in soak\\n  - Timeline / activity panel (steps, approvals, auto-stop events)\\n  - Cohort metric comparisons\\n  - Actions: Start, Pause, Resume, Advance step, Rollback\\n\\n#### Rollout orchestration\\n- State machine supports: create \\u2192 start \\u2192 progress steps \\u2192 complete, plus pause/resume and rollback.\\n- Step progression must enforce minimum soak time and approval gating.\\n- Rollback must be idempotent and fast (target: < 2 minutes to fully enforce 0% canary globally for the route, excluding client caching).\\n\\n#### Routing enforcement\\n- Percentage split enforcement by route + active rollout.\\n- Deterministic cohort assignment (sticky per end-user/request key as defined in ADR) to avoid flapping between baseline/canary.\\n- Must handle streaming and retries consistently (same cohort selection on retry where possible).\\n- Multi-region behavior: percentage applies per region unless explicitly configured; the GA default is per-region enforcement with consistent semantics and no cross-region coordination dependency.\\n\\n#### Observability and metrics\\n- Requests must be tagged with `rollout_id` and `cohort` (baseline/canary) for aggregation.\\n- Provide standard dashboard views (Console and internal) for:\\n  - error rate (5xx)\\n  - timeout rate\\n  - p50/p95 latency\\n  - tokens/sec (or throughput proxy)\\n  - request volume\\n- Comparisons should show baseline vs canary deltas with clear labeling and guidance.\\n\\n#### Audit logs\\n- Emit audit log events for: create, update schedule, start, pause, resume, approve, step change, auto-stop triggered, rollback, complete.\\n- Each event includes: actor identity, tenant, route, rollout_id, before/after (diff summary), timestamp, and source (Console/API/system).\\n\\n### Guardrails (policy requirements)\\nGuardrails are evaluated at action-time (e.g., when starting or advancing a step) and surfaced in Console as clear, actionable errors.\\n\\n#### Default guardrail baseline (GA defaults)\\nThe following are defaults; they may be overridden by tenant tier/entitlement and org admin policy.\\n\\n| Guardrail | Default | Notes |\\n|---|---:|---|\\n| Max step size increase | 25 percentage points | Example: 5% \\u2192 50% is denied; 25% \\u2192 50% allowed. |\\n| Minimum soak time per step | 15 minutes | Soak timer starts when split is confirmed active. |\\n| Approval required at/above | 25% canary | Approval required to go to 25% and above (including 25%). |\\n| Approval role | rollout-approver | Separate from operator role; org-defined membership. |\\n| Rollback permission | rollout-operator (and above) | Emergency rollback should not be blocked by approval gates. |\\n| Auto-stop enabled | On by default | Customers can tune thresholds within allowed bounds. |\\n\\n#### Stop condition defaults (GA defaults)\\nStop conditions evaluate using cohort-tagged metrics. Defaults aim to be safe and avoid noise in low-volume scenarios.\\n\\nAll stop conditions should include a **minimum sample requirement** to avoid acting on tiny traffic: default `min_requests = 500` per cohort in the evaluation window, adjustable by tier.\\n\\n| Stop condition | Default threshold | Evaluation window | Action |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| 5xx error rate regression | canary_error_rate > max(0.5%, 1.5x baseline_error_rate) | 5 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify; optional auto-rollback if persists 10 minutes. |\\n| Timeout rate regression | canary_timeout_rate > max(0.3%, 2.0x baseline_timeout_rate) | 5 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify. |\\n| p95 latency regression | canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.30 AND (canary_p95 - baseline_p95) > 100ms | 10 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify. |\\n\\nNotes:\\n- Auto-rollback behavior is tier-gated for GA: default is **auto-pause**, with **auto-rollback** allowed for tenants with \\u201cAdvanced Rollout Safety\\u201d entitlement (or by support enablement during beta).\\n- Stop conditions must be visible in the rollout timeline with the specific rule that triggered.\\n\\n### Permissions and entitlements (GA)\\n- Console must respect RBAC:\\n  - `rollout:create`\\n  - `rollout:start`\\n  - `rollout:pause`\\n  - `rollout:resume`\\n  - `rollout:advance_step`\\n  - `rollout:approve`\\n  - `rollout:rollback`\\n  - `rollout:view`\\n- The \\u201crollout-approver\\u201d role must be supported and auditable.\\n\\n### API requirements (GA)\\n- Provide backend endpoints used by Console (and available as public API if already aligned with product direction):\\n  - Create rollout (draft)\\n  - Validate rollout (policy + schema)\\n  - Start rollout\\n  - Pause / Resume\\n  - Advance step / Set target percentage (within policy)\\n  - Rollback\\n  - Get rollout status + timeline + metrics links\\n- Errors must include:\\n  - stable error codes\\n  - user-friendly messages\\n  - policy violation details (e.g., \\u201cmax_step_increase_exceeded: attempted 45pp > allowed 25pp\\u201d)\\n\\n### UX requirements (GA)\\n- Clear warnings for risky actions:\\n  - Large step changes\\n  - Disabling auto-stop\\n  - Starting rollouts without enough baseline traffic to compare\\n- Destructive actions (Rollback, Cancel) require confirmation with explicit consequences.\\n- Timeline view must answer:\\n  - What is the current canary %?\\n  - What happened (start/pause/approval/auto-stop)?\\n  - Who did it?\\n  - What is next and when?\\n\\n## Success metrics\\n### Customer outcomes (leading indicators)\\n- At least 10 customers successfully run Hosted canary rollouts end-to-end in the first 60 days post-GA.\\n- Median time to rollback (from action to enforcement) under 2 minutes for \\u2265 p95 of rollbacks.\\n- Reduction in \\u201cunsafe change\\u201d incidents attributable to route updates (baseline vs post-GA quarter), measured via incident tagging.\\n\\n### Product health / reliability\\n- Rollout workflow service availability meets or exceeds Console backend SLOs (target: 99.9% monthly for core APIs).\\n- Auto-stop false-positive rate is tracked; target: < 5% of auto-stops later deemed \\u201cunnecessary\\u201d after review (beta + first GA quarter).\\n- Telemetry cardinality remains within budget; no sustained metrics ingestion incidents caused by rollout tags.\\n\\n### Adoption / engagement\\n- % of eligible tenants with feature enabled who create at least one rollout within 30 days.\\n- Completion rate of rollouts (created \\u2192 completed) and reasons for abandonment (manual pause, rollback, validation errors).\\n\\n## Rollout plan (beta \\u2192 GA)\\n### Phase 0: Internal dogfood (1\\u20132 weeks)\\n- Enable for Redwood internal tenants and staging.\\n- Run scripted rollouts on a test route with synthetic load.\\n- Validate: cohorting correctness, step transitions, stop conditions, and audit logs.\\n\\n### Phase 1: Design partner beta (2\\u20136 weeks)\\n- Enable for a small set of customers (per-tenant feature flag).\\n- Weekly check-ins; collect feedback on:\\n  - wizard clarity\\n  - metric comparison usefulness\\n  - policy defaults (step size, soak, approvals)\\n  - stop condition sensitivity\\n- SRE monitors split correctness and metric evaluation latency.\\n\\n### Phase 2: Limited GA (1\\u20132 weeks)\\n- Expand enablement by tier/segment.\\n- Keep a kill switch that disables new rollouts and/or forces rollouts into paused state if needed.\\n\\n### Phase 3: Full GA\\n- Default on for eligible Hosted tenants (subject to tier and account settings).\\n- Publish docs and release notes; support trained on common issues.\\n\\n## GA acceptance criteria\\nA feature is GA-ready when:\\n1. End-to-end workflow is stable in production for multiple tenants (create \\u2192 start \\u2192 step \\u2192 approval \\u2192 auto-stop \\u2192 rollback).\\n2. Deterministic cohorting verified (no sustained split mismatch beyond expected statistical variance; clear tolerance thresholds documented in SRE doc).\\n3. Audit events complete and consistent with security spec; events visible to customers in timeline.\\n4. Stop conditions trigger correctly and do not cause widespread false positives; evaluation timeouts handled (rollout does not get stuck indefinitely).\\n5. Documentation complete (Console walkthrough + API + troubleshooting).\\n6. On-call runbook exists and has been exercised at least once in a simulated incident.\\n\\n## Dependencies\\n- Smart Routing/data plane support for percentage split enforcement and cohort tagging.\\n- Control plane schema and policy engine for guardrails.\\n- Telemetry pipeline support for cohort-level aggregations within cardinality constraints.\\n- RBAC policy bundle updates (rollout-approver role).\\n\\n## Risks and mitigations\\n1. **Traffic split mismatch (routing bug or regional drift)**\\n   - Mitigation: deterministic hashing, automated split verification checks in staging; runbook and kill switch.\\n2. **Telemetry cardinality / cost blow-ups**\\n   - Mitigation: fixed tags only (`rollout_id`, `cohort`, `route`, `region`), sampling policies, and TTL for high-cardinality rollout IDs in some views.\\n3. **Stop condition tuning (too sensitive or not sensitive enough)**\\n   - Mitigation: minimum sample requirements; default to auto-pause; tier-gated auto-rollback; post-beta tuning.\\n4. **Governance complexity (approvals vs emergency response)**\\n   - Mitigation: rollback always allowed to operators; approvals required only for increasing risk (higher %), not for safety actions.\\n\\n## Open questions\\n- What is the exact stickiness key for cohorting in Hosted for common SDK usage (API key + user id header + request id fallback)? Confirm final ADR alignment.\\n- Do we allow customer-defined step schedules with arbitrary percentages, or restrict to a recommended ladder (1/5/10/25/50/100) for GA?\\n- Do we expose public API for rollouts in GA, or keep API \\u201cConsole-backed\\u201d while we finalize external API naming/versioning?\\n\\n## Known gaps / follow-ups (post-GA candidates)\\n- Quality gates integrated with Redwood Optimize evals (automated gating based on prompt sets and regression thresholds).\\n- Dedicated/Private parity (same workflow, same policy schema, same timeline view).\\n- Multi-variant rollouts (A/B/n) and dynamic routing optimizations.\\n- More granular stop conditions (model-level tokenization errors, tool-calling failure rate, structured output validity rate).\\n- Per-route \\u201csafe defaults\\u201d wizard presets and recommended schedules based on traffic volume.\\n\\n## Appendix: Example rollout schedule\\nRecommended default schedule for first-time rollouts:\\n1. 1% for 30 minutes\\n2. 5% for 30 minutes\\n3. 25% for 60 minutes (approval required)\\n4. 50% for 60 minutes (approval required)\\n5. 100% (approval required)\\n\\n## Appendix: Customer messaging (GA)\\n- \\u201cSafely roll out a new model version or configuration on Hosted routes with percentage traffic splitting, built-in guardrails, and one-click rollback.\\u201d\\n- \\u201cCompare baseline vs canary latency and error rates, and maintain governance with approvals and audit logs.\\u201d\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_63abd3750ce94b12aebc0d25c1f3c45b\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: PRD: Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: product-docs\n\nbody : # # summary redwood inference is shipping a ga “ hosted canary rollout workflow ” that allows customers to safely introduce a new model version and / or serving configuration on an existing * hosted route * by gradually shifting traffic via percentage splits ( e. g., 1 % → 5 % → 25 % → 50 % → 100 % ). this prd covers the customer workflow in redwood console, the underlying rollout orchestration model, routing enforcement, telemetry / stop conditions, auditability, and the ga bar.",

{
  "title": "PRD: Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA)",
  "space": "product-docs",
  "author": "Marissa Cole",
  "owner_team": "product",
  "status": "in_review",
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "created_at": "2025-03-12",
  "last_updated": "2025-04-08",
  "reviewers": [
    "Paula Mendes",
    "Dylan Brooks",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Tessa Morgan",
    "Elliot Price"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "hosted",
    "console",
    "rollouts",
    "canary",
    "ga",
    "policy",
    "observability",
    "audit-logs"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-rollout-policy-evaluation-order-and-precedence.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/rollout-orchestrator-service.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts.json",
    "sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/console-release-notes-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga.json"
  ],
  "body": "## Summary
Redwood Inference is shipping a GA “Hosted canary rollout workflow” that allows customers to safely introduce a new model version and/or serving configuration on an existing *Hosted route* by gradually shifting traffic via percentage splits (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%).

This PRD covers the customer workflow in Redwood Console, the underlying rollout orchestration model, routing enforcement, telemetry/stop conditions, auditability, and the GA bar.

## Problem statement
Customers operating production LLM workloads need a safe and auditable path to change model versions and serving configs (quantization, prompt templates, tool/function calling settings, safety filters, etc.). Today, most customers rely on ad-hoc approaches:
- “Big bang” route updates with manual rollback when issues occur.
- Parallel routes and client-side traffic splitting.
- Custom scripts to change model versions during low-traffic windows.

These approaches increase the risk of outages and quality regressions, slow down iteration, and reduce confidence in deploying improvements.

### Why now
- We already have primitives (model versioning, routing policies, observability) but lack a cohesive, GA-ready workflow with guardrails and rollback.
- Enterprise prospects and regulated customers are explicitly asking for: approvals, audit logs, and change control evidence.

## Goals (GA scope)
1. Provide a Console workflow to create, run, pause, and rollback canary rollouts on *Hosted routes*.
2. Provide policy guardrails to ensure safe rollouts: max step size, minimum soak time, approval gates, and automatic stop/rollback on SLO breaches.
3. Provide customer-visible transparency: rollout timeline + cohort metric comparisons (baseline vs canary).
4. Emit complete audit logs for rollout actions.
5. Ensure the implementation is reliable, observable, and operable by on-call.

## Non-goals (explicitly out of GA scope)
- Multi-armed bandits or automatic traffic optimization.
- Fully automated quality-eval gating as a hard requirement (quality metrics may be displayed or optionally provided as manual inputs).
- GA parity for Dedicated/Private workflows (schema compatibility is required, but Hosted is the GA target).

## Target users / personas
- **ML Engineer / Platform Engineer (primary):** needs safe rollout tooling, metrics comparisons, quick rollback.
- **SRE / Reliability Engineer (secondary):** needs SLO-based auto-stop, low-noise alerting, clear runbooks.
- **Security / Compliance (secondary):** needs audit logs, approvals, role-based permissions, retention/export posture.

## User stories
### Create and run a canary rollout
1. As a user, I can select a Hosted route and choose a baseline and canary model version/config.
2. As a user, I can define a traffic schedule (step list) and see validation/warnings if it violates policy.
3. As a user, I can start a rollout and watch baseline vs canary metrics and the rollout timeline.

### Safety and change control
4. As an org admin, I can enforce guardrails (max % step, min soak time, approvals required) per tenant/tier.
5. As a rollout operator, I can pause a rollout and resume later.
6. As a rollout operator, I can rollback immediately to 0% canary (100% baseline) and lock the rollout to prevent accidental re-advance.
7. As a compliance reviewer, I can see an audit trail of who did what, when, and what changed.

### Automatic protection
8. As a customer, I can configure (or accept defaults for) stop conditions so that a rollout pauses or rolls back on error/latency regressions.
9. As Redwood SRE, I can trust that stop conditions do not produce alert storms and that we have enough telemetry to diagnose false positives.

## Definitions
- **Hosted route:** Customer-facing API endpoint in Redwood Hosted (e.g., `/v1/chat/completions` route mapped to a model/version/config).
- **Baseline:** The currently serving model/version/config for the route.
- **Canary:** The candidate model/version/config introduced during rollout.
- **Cohort:** Baseline vs canary traffic buckets used for metric comparisons.
- **Step:** Target canary traffic percentage for a time window (soak).

## Requirements
### Functional requirements (GA)
#### Console workflow
- Provide a wizard-like flow:
  1) Select route
  2) Choose baseline and canary (model version + config)
  3) Configure schedule (steps + soak times)
  4) Configure guardrails / stop conditions (as allowed)
  5) Review + confirm
- Provide a rollout detail page with:
  - Current state (Draft/Running/Paused/Completed/Rolled back/Failed)
  - Current step target and time remaining in soak
  - Timeline / activity panel (steps, approvals, auto-stop events)
  - Cohort metric comparisons
  - Actions: Start, Pause, Resume, Advance step, Rollback

#### Rollout orchestration
- State machine supports: create → start → progress steps → complete, plus pause/resume and rollback.
- Step progression must enforce minimum soak time and approval gating.
- Rollback must be idempotent and fast (target: < 2 minutes to fully enforce 0% canary globally for the route, excluding client caching).

#### Routing enforcement
- Percentage split enforcement by route + active rollout.
- Deterministic cohort assignment (sticky per end-user/request key as defined in ADR) to avoid flapping between baseline/canary.
- Must handle streaming and retries consistently (same cohort selection on retry where possible).
- Multi-region behavior: percentage applies per region unless explicitly configured; the GA default is per-region enforcement with consistent semantics and no cross-region coordination dependency.

#### Observability and metrics
- Requests must be tagged with `rollout_id` and `cohort` (baseline/canary) for aggregation.
- Provide standard dashboard views (Console and internal) for:
  - error rate (5xx)
  - timeout rate
  - p50/p95 latency
  - tokens/sec (or throughput proxy)
  - request volume
- Comparisons should show baseline vs canary deltas with clear labeling and guidance.

#### Audit logs
- Emit audit log events for: create, update schedule, start, pause, resume, approve, step change, auto-stop triggered, rollback, complete.
- Each event includes: actor identity, tenant, route, rollout_id, before/after (diff summary), timestamp, and source (Console/API/system).

### Guardrails (policy requirements)
Guardrails are evaluated at action-time (e.g., when starting or advancing a step) and surfaced in Console as clear, actionable errors.

#### Default guardrail baseline (GA defaults)
The following are defaults; they may be overridden by tenant tier/entitlement and org admin policy.

| Guardrail | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Max step size increase | 25 percentage points | Example: 5% → 50% is denied; 25% → 50% allowed. |
| Minimum soak time per step | 15 minutes | Soak timer starts when split is confirmed active. |
| Approval required at/above | 25% canary | Approval required to go to 25% and above (including 25%). |
| Approval role | rollout-approver | Separate from operator role; org-defined membership. |
| Rollback permission | rollout-operator (and above) | Emergency rollback should not be blocked by approval gates. |
| Auto-stop enabled | On by default | Customers can tune thresholds within allowed bounds. |

#### Stop condition defaults (GA defaults)
Stop conditions evaluate using cohort-tagged metrics. Defaults aim to be safe and avoid noise in low-volume scenarios.

All stop conditions should include a **minimum sample requirement** to avoid acting on tiny traffic: default `min_requests = 500` per cohort in the evaluation window, adjustable by tier.

| Stop condition | Default threshold | Evaluation window | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5xx error rate regression | canary_error_rate > max(0.5%, 1.5x baseline_error_rate) | 5 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify; optional auto-rollback if persists 10 minutes. |
| Timeout rate regression | canary_timeout_rate > max(0.3%, 2.0x baseline_timeout_rate) | 5 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify. |
| p95 latency regression | canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.30 AND (canary_p95 - baseline_p95) > 100ms | 10 minutes | Auto-pause rollout and notify. |

Notes:
- Auto-rollback behavior is tier-gated for GA: default is **auto-pause**, with **auto-rollback** allowed for tenants with “Advanced Rollout Safety” entitlement (or by support enablement during beta).
- Stop conditions must be visible in the rollout timeline with the specific rule that triggered.

### Permissions and entitlements (GA)
- Console must respect RBAC:
  - `rollout:create`
  - `rollout:start`
  - `rollout:pause`
  - `rollout:resume`
  - `rollout:advance_step`
  - `rollout:approve`
  - `rollout:rollback`
  - `rollout:view`
- The “rollout-approver” role must be supported and auditable.

### API requirements (GA)
- Provide backend endpoints used by Console (and available as public API if already aligned with product direction):
  - Create rollout (draft)
  - Validate rollout (policy + schema)
  - Start rollout
  - Pause / Resume
  - Advance step / Set target percentage (within policy)
  - Rollback
  - Get rollout status + timeline + metrics links
- Errors must include:
  - stable error codes
  - user-friendly messages
  - policy violation details (e.g., “max_step_increase_exceeded: attempted 45pp > allowed 25pp”)

### UX requirements (GA)
- Clear warnings for risky actions:
  - Large step changes
  - Disabling auto-stop
  - Starting rollouts without enough baseline traffic to compare
- Destructive actions (Rollback, Cancel) require confirmation with explicit consequences.
- Timeline view must answer:
  - What is the current canary %?
  - What happened (start/pause/approval/auto-stop)?
  - Who did it?
  - What is next and when?

## Success metrics
### Customer outcomes (leading indicators)
- At least 10 customers successfully run Hosted canary rollouts end-to-end in the first 60 days post-GA.
- Median time to rollback (from action to enforcement) under 2 minutes for ≥ p95 of rollbacks.
- Reduction in “unsafe change” incidents attributable to route updates (baseline vs post-GA quarter), measured via incident tagging.

### Product health / reliability
- Rollout workflow service availability meets or exceeds Console backend SLOs (target: 99.9% monthly for core APIs).
- Auto-stop false-positive rate is tracked; target: < 5% of auto-stops later deemed “unnecessary” after review (beta + first GA quarter).
- Telemetry cardinality remains within budget; no sustained metrics ingestion incidents caused by rollout tags.

### Adoption / engagement
- % of eligible tenants with feature enabled who create at least one rollout within 30 days.
- Completion rate of rollouts (created → completed) and reasons for abandonment (manual pause, rollback, validation errors).

## Rollout plan (beta → GA)
### Phase 0: Internal dogfood (1–2 weeks)
- Enable for Redwood internal tenants and staging.
- Run scripted rollouts on a test route with synthetic load.
- Validate: cohorting correctness, step transitions, stop conditions, and audit logs.

### Phase 1: Design partner beta (2–6 weeks)
- Enable for a small set of customers (per-tenant feature flag).
- Weekly check-ins; collect feedback on:
  - wizard clarity
  - metric comparison usefulness
  - policy defaults (step size, soak, approvals)
  - stop condition sensitivity
- SRE monitors split correctness and metric evaluation latency.

### Phase 2: Limited GA (1–2 weeks)
- Expand enablement by tier/segment.
- Keep a kill switch that disables new rollouts and/or forces rollouts into paused state if needed.

### Phase 3: Full GA
- Default on for eligible Hosted tenants (subject to tier and account settings).
- Publish docs and release notes; support trained on common issues.

## GA acceptance criteria
A feature is GA-ready when:
1. End-to-end workflow is stable in production for multiple tenants (create → start → step → approval → auto-stop → rollback).
2. Deterministic cohorting verified (no sustained split mismatch beyond expected statistical variance; clear tolerance thresholds documented in SRE doc).
3. Audit events complete and consistent with security spec; events visible to customers in timeline.
4. Stop conditions trigger correctly and do not cause widespread false positives; evaluation timeouts handled (rollout does not get stuck indefinitely).
5. Documentation complete (Console walkthrough + API + troubleshooting).
6. On-call runbook exists and has been exercised at least once in a simulated incident.

## Dependencies
- Smart Routing/data plane support for percentage split enforcement and cohort tagging.
- Control plane schema and policy engine for guardrails.
- Telemetry pipeline support for cohort-level aggregations within cardinality constraints.
- RBAC policy bundle updates (rollout-approver role).

## Risks and mitigations
1. **Traffic split mismatch (routing bug or regional drift)**
   - Mitigation: deterministic hashing, automated split verification checks in staging; runbook and kill switch.
2. **Telemetry cardinality / cost blow-ups**
   - Mitigation: fixed tags only (`rollout_id`, `cohort`, `route`, `region`), sampling policies, and TTL for high-cardinality rollout IDs in some views.
3. **Stop condition tuning (too sensitive or not sensitive enough)**
   - Mitigation: minimum sample requirements; default to auto-pause; tier-gated auto-rollback; post-beta tuning.
4. **Governance complexity (approvals vs emergency response)**
   - Mitigation: rollback always allowed to operators; approvals required only for increasing risk (higher %), not for safety actions.

## Open questions
- What is the exact stickiness key for cohorting in Hosted for common SDK usage (API key + user id header + request id fallback)? Confirm final ADR alignment.
- Do we allow customer-defined step schedules with arbitrary percentages, or restrict to a recommended ladder (1/5/10/25/50/100) for GA?
- Do we expose public API for rollouts in GA, or keep API “Console-backed” while we finalize external API naming/versioning?

## Known gaps / follow-ups (post-GA candidates)
- Quality gates integrated with Redwood Optimize evals (automated gating based on prompt sets and regression thresholds).
- Dedicated/Private parity (same workflow, same policy schema, same timeline view).
- Multi-variant rollouts (A/B/n) and dynamic routing optimizations.
- More granular stop conditions (model-level tokenization errors, tool-calling failure rate, structured output validity rate).
- Per-route “safe defaults” wizard presets and recommended schedules based on traffic volume.

## Appendix: Example rollout schedule
Recommended default schedule for first-time rollouts:
1. 1% for 30 minutes
2. 5% for 30 minutes
3. 25% for 60 minutes (approval required)
4. 50% for 60 minutes (approval required)
5. 100% (approval required)

## Appendix: Customer messaging (GA)
- “Safely roll out a new model version or configuration on Hosted routes with percentage traffic splitting, built-in guardrails, and one-click rollback.”
- “Compare baseline vs canary latency and error rates, and maintain governance with approvals and audit logs.”

paging unless systemic).\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)\\n- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)\\n\\nD) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)\\nOwner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei\\nRequired audit event coverage\\n- Events must be emitted for:\\n  - rollout.created\\n  - rollout.started\\n  - rollout.step.approval_requested\\n  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied\\n  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)\\n  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed\\n  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)\\n  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)\\n  - rollout.completed\\n- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state \\u2192 new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.\\n- Retention and export:\\n  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier\\n  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)\\n\\nCustomer-visible activity timeline\\n- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show \\u201cwhat happened\\u201d and \\u201cwhy\\u201d (e.g., auto-pause reason).\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)\\n- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)\\n\\nE) Policy guardrails + RBAC\\nOwner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen\\n- Guardrails enforced for step changes:\\n  - Max step size (e.g., 1% \\u2192 50% disallowed without override/approval)\\n  - Minimum soak time before next step\\n  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy\\n- Entitlement mapping documented:\\n  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.\\n- RBAC roles validated:\\n  - Who can create rollouts\\n  - Who can start/pause/rollback\\n  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)\\n- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., \\u201cWait 20m more to satisfy min soak\\u201d)\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)\\n- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups\\n\\nF) Documentation (public + internal)\\nOwner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen\\nCustomer docs must include\\n- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time\\n- Step-by-step Console walkthrough\\n- API reference (or links) for rollout operations\\n- Troubleshooting:\\n  - Why a rollout auto-paused\\n  - Why metrics show \\u201cinsufficient volume\\u201d\\n  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)\\n  - How to rollback safely\\n- Limitations (GA):\\n  - No bandits/dynamic optimization\\n  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)\\n  - Dedicated/Private not GA\\n\\nInternal docs must include\\n- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)\\n- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split\\n- Release/change management checklist\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)\\n- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support\\n\\nG) Support readiness + incident response\\nOwner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes\\n- Support playbooks:\\n  - Triage flow for \\u201crollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike\\u201d\\n  - Triage flow for \\u201ctraffic split not matching config\\u201d\\n  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering\\n  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs\\n- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., \\u201cHow do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?\\u201d)\\n- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)\\n- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)\\n\\nH) Release management + staged rollout plan\\nOwner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee\\n- Feature flags:\\n  - Per-tenant enablement\\n  - Internal dogfood tenants first\\n  - Staged cohort of beta \\u2192 expanded beta \\u2192 GA default (if applicable)\\n  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)\\n- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes\\n- Backout strategy:\\n  - Disable canary UI\\n  - Force baseline routing\\n  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts\\n\\nAcceptance evidence\\n- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)\\n- Release readiness review held 48\\u201372 hours pre-GA\\n\\nGo/No-Go Process (how we decide)\\nMeeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)\\nRequired attendees / signoffs\\n- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)\\n- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin\\n- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee\\n- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad\\n- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes\\n- Security: Marcus Lin\\n- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel\\n\\nDecision rules\\n- No-go if any of:\\n  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates\\n  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable\\n  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above\\n  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved\\n  - No validated kill switch\\n- Conditional go allowed if:\\n  - Minor UI polish issues only\\n  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date\\n  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)\\n\\nArtifacts to attach in go/no-go notes\\n- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs\\n- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot\\n- List of webhook). document.title: GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-1859",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "GA launch criteria + beta exit checklist — Hosted canary rollouts",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-22",
  "creator": "Paula Mendes",
  "assignee": "Marissa Cole",
  "project": "Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow (GA)",
  "cycle": "2025-W12",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-04-04",
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2025.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "labels": [
    "ga-readiness",
    "hosted",
    "rollouts",
    "console",
    "sre",
    "security",
    "docs",
    "support-enablement"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "PM-1843",
    "PM-1851",
    "ENG-9123",
    "ENG-9140",
    "ENG-9146",
    "ENG-9152",
    "ENG-9158",
    "ENG-9171",
    "ENG-9180",
    "DES-742",
    "DES-755",
    "DES-763"
  ],
  "sub_issues": [
    "Create GA go/no-go doc + signoff list (Console/Platform/SRE/Security/Support)",
    "Confirm default auto-stop thresholds by tier/region for GA",
    "Finalize customer-facing limitations/known issues section for docs",
    "Support macros + troubleshooting flow for auto-pause / split mismatch",
    "Run GA staging game day with stop/rollback + audit validation"
  ],
  "description": "Purpose
- Define the Beta Exit criteria and GA Launch checklist for the Hosted canary rollout workflow (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes).
- Align Console, Control Plane, Smart Routing/Data Plane, Telemetry/SRE, Security, Docs, and Support on what “GA-ready” means.
- Serve as the single checklist for the GA go/no-go meeting and as a record of what we validated.

Scope reminder (GA)
- Hosted routes only (Dedicated/Private: schema-compatible, not GA)
- Console wizard to create/run/pause/rollback, plus timeline/activity view and cohort comparison metrics
- Policy guardrails: max step size, min soak time, approval gates (RBAC), auto-stop/auto-rollback based on SLO metrics
- Audit logging + customer-visible activity timeline

Beta Exit Criteria (must meet before scheduling GA)
1) Design partner validation
- Minimum: 5 design partners enabled, with at least 3 running a real production canary on Hosted.
- At least 10 completed rollouts end-to-end (create → start → step changes → reach 100% OR rollback).
- No P0/P1 issues open related to incorrect routing split, inability to rollback, or audit trail gaps.
- Qualitative: partners confirm they can understand (a) current step, (b) what will happen next, (c) why auto-stop occurred, and (d) how to rollback.

2) Reliability outcomes during beta
- No unresolved incidents attributable to rollout feature causing widespread request misrouting or outages.
- Any beta incidents have documented root cause, fix merged, and backported as needed (e.g., metric timeout stall bugfix; split mismatch learnings).
- SRE signoff that alerts are actionable and not generating sustained alert storms.

3) Governance + safety outcomes during beta
- Policy guardrails enforced consistently across UI and API (no bypass via API for restricted actions).
- Approval gates tested with RBAC role(s) (rollout-approver) and common enterprise setups.
- Audit events present for all required action types, with correct actor identity and diffs.

GA Launch Checklist (go/no-go)
A) Functional completeness (Console + API)
Owner: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Wizard flow supports:
  - Selecting route, baseline model version/config, canary model version/config
  - Defining traffic schedule (step %, soak duration)
  - Configuring guardrails (max step size, min soak time) and showing validation errors clearly
  - Review + confirm with explicit warnings for destructive actions (rollback)
- Lifecycle actions supported and validated end-to-end:
  - Create rollout (draft)
  - Start rollout
  - Progress to next step (with/without approval gate)
  - Pause/resume
  - Rollback (manual) and “rollback to baseline” semantics
  - Auto-pause / auto-rollback on SLO breach (with reason surfaced)
- State machine correctness:
  - No “stuck” states on metric evaluation timeouts; clear retry + user-facing error
  - Idempotent retries for control plane → data plane propagation
- API parity for core operations (documented): create, get status, list activity, approve step, pause/resume, rollback

Acceptance evidence
- E2E test suite passing in CI and nightly (ENG-9164)
- Staging manual walkthrough recorded (link in go/no-go notes)

B) Smart Routing enforcement correctness
Owner: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Deterministic cohorting implemented and documented (hash inputs + stickiness rules)
- Percentage split accuracy within tolerance per region (define tolerance below)
- Correct behavior for:
  - Multi-region traffic
  - Streaming requests
  - Retries (client and internal)
  - Fallback routing interactions (baseline vs canary; precedence per ADR)
- Kill switch behavior verified:
  - Tenant-level disable immediately forces 100% baseline
  - Global disable forces baseline and prevents new rollouts from starting

Split accuracy target (GA)
- For stable traffic volume, measured canary proportion should converge to target within ±2% absolute over a 15-minute window (per region), excluding low-volume routes.
- For low volume routes, UI must display “insufficient volume” guidance instead of implying precise percentages.

Acceptance evidence
- Staging smoke tests (perf-canary PR-147)
- Post-fix validation for beta split mismatch scenario (see incident thread: rollout-split-mismatch-us-east)

C) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting
Owner: Sean Gallagher / Aisha Bello / Logan Wright
Required cohort signals (tagging + aggregation)
- Every request must be attributable to:
  - route
  - model version/config (baseline vs canary)
  - cohort (baseline/canary)
  - region
  - rollout_id (with cardinality controls; ensure no blowups)
- Metrics required in Console comparison view + internal dashboards:
  - Request rate (RPS)
  - Error rate (overall, 5xx, timeouts)
  - Latency (p50/p95; ideally p99 in internal)
  - Tokens/sec and cost proxies (where available)
  - Streaming-specific failure modes (disconnects, partial completions) if tracked

Stop conditions (GA defaults)
- Auto-stop/auto-rollback must be available and enabled by default for new rollouts (with ability to tune thresholds by entitlement/tier).
- Default thresholds (initial GA proposal; finalize with SRE):
  - 5xx error rate: canary exceeds baseline by +1.0% absolute AND exceeds 2.0% absolute for 5 minutes
  - Timeout rate: canary exceeds baseline by +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency regression: canary p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 for 10 minutes (guard for low volume)
- Rollout behavior on breach:
  - Auto-pause first if we can attribute breach confidently; auto-rollback when breach persists (or per policy)
  - Always emit: (1) customer-visible timeline entry, (2) audit event, (3) notification event

Alerting guidelines
- Alerts should page SRE only for:
  - Routing enforcement drift/incorrectness
  - Orchestrator stuck rollouts at scale
  - Global cohort tagging failures
  - Control plane → data plane propagation failures
- Customer route-specific canary SLO breaches should notify customer in Console/timeline and optionally via webhook/email (no paging unless systemic).

Acceptance evidence
- Cohort dashboards exist + validated against known traffic patterns (PR-28910 / observability pack PR-184)
- Cardinality analysis completed and within limits (Drive: rollout-cohort-metrics-cardinality-analysis)

D) Audit logging + change history (Security/Compliance)
Owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
Required audit event coverage
- Events must be emitted for:
  - rollout.created
  - rollout.started
  - rollout.step.approval_requested
  - rollout.step.approved / rollout.step.denied
  - rollout.step.changed (percent change)
  - rollout.paused / rollout.resumed
  - rollout.rolled_back (manual)
  - rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back (include stop condition + metric snapshot reference)
  - rollout.completed
- Required fields (high level): tenant_id, actor_id/actor_type, route_id, rollout_id, previous_state → new_state, diff (human readable + structured), timestamp, request_id/trace_id when applicable.
- Retention and export:
  - Align with existing audit log retention policy by tier
  - Verify SIEM export compatibility (field naming and size limits)

Customer-visible activity timeline
- Must match audit events but may exclude security-only internal fields; should show “what happened” and “why” (e.g., auto-pause reason).

Acceptance evidence
- Security review of audit event schema doc (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)
- Sample events captured in staging and validated by Security (screenshots/log dumps referenced in go/no-go)

E) Policy guardrails + RBAC
Owner: Jordan Lee / Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Guardrails enforced for step changes:
  - Max step size (e.g., 1% → 50% disallowed without override/approval)
  - Minimum soak time before next step
  - Approval gates configurable by tenant/admin policy
- Entitlement mapping documented:
  - Which customers get auto-rollback, approvals, advanced retention, etc.
- RBAC roles validated:
  - Who can create rollouts
  - Who can start/pause/rollback
  - Who can approve (rollout-approver role)
- UI error messaging must reflect policy engine errors with actionable guidance (e.g., “Wait 20m more to satisfy min soak”)

Acceptance evidence
- Policy engine tests and Console integration tests pass (PR-28802)
- Manual validation with at least 2 common enterprise role setups

F) Documentation (public + internal)
Owner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
Customer docs must include
- Conceptual overview: baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time
- Step-by-step Console walkthrough
- API reference (or links) for rollout operations
- Troubleshooting:
  - Why a rollout auto-paused
  - Why metrics show “insufficient volume”
  - Split mismatch debugging steps (what to check before contacting support)
  - How to rollback safely
- Limitations (GA):
  - No bandits/dynamic optimization
  - Quality gates optional/manual (not hard gates)
  - Dedicated/Private not GA

Internal docs must include
- Enablement how-to (feature flags, permissions, sanity checks)
- On-call runbook for stuck rollout / bad split
- Release/change management checklist

Acceptance evidence
- Docs PR merged (redwood-docs PR-922)
- Runbooks published (Confluence) and reviewed with SRE + Support

G) Support readiness + incident response
Owner: Dev Patel / Rafael Mendes
- Support playbooks:
  - Triage flow for “rollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike”
  - Triage flow for “traffic split not matching config”
  - Escalation path to on-call / engineering
  - What data to request: tenant_id, route, rollout_id, timeframe, region, request IDs
- Macros/snippets created for common questions (e.g., “How do I do a percentage rollout on Hosted route?”)
- SLA for response during GA launch week and ownership for escalation channel

Acceptance evidence
- At least 2 support training sessions run (recording link in go/no-go)
- Sample tickets resolved using new macros (reference: SUP-48211, SUP-48302, SUP-48377)

H) Release management + staged rollout plan
Owner: Connor O'Brien / Soojin Lee
- Feature flags:
  - Per-tenant enablement
  - Internal dogfood tenants first
  - Staged cohort of beta → expanded beta → GA default (if applicable)
  - Kill switch playbook (owners + steps)
- Migration/backward compatibility validated for config schema changes
- Backout strategy:
  - Disable canary UI
  - Force baseline routing
  - Preserve audit logs and rollout history for completed rollouts

Acceptance evidence
- Change management checklist completed (Drive: hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist)
- Release readiness review held 48–72 hours pre-GA

Go/No-Go Process (how we decide)
Meeting: GA Readiness Review (60 minutes)
Required attendees / signoffs
- Product: Marissa Cole (final call)
- Console Eng: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Platform/Policy: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad
- SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes
- Security: Marcus Lin
- Docs/Support: Elliot Price + Dev Patel

Decision rules
- No-go if any of:
  - Known issue causing incorrect split enforcement at material rates
  - Rollback unavailable or unreliable
  - Missing audit events for any action type listed above
  - Unbounded metrics cardinality risk unresolved
  - No validated kill switch
- Conditional go allowed if:
  - Minor UI polish issues only
  - Non-blocking docs follow-ups with explicit owner + date
  - Non-paging alert tuning improvements queued (does not impact safety)

Artifacts to attach in go/no-go notes
- Links: PRD, design spec, ADRs
- Latest beta partner tracker snapshot
- List of open bugs (P0/P1 only) with owners + ETA
- Staging game day results + any follow-ups

Current status / open questions (as of last update)
- Need final agreement on GA default thresholds by region/tier; beta feedback suggests p95 multiplier threshold may be too aggressive for long-context routes.
- Confirm whether GA requires customer notifications beyond Console timeline (e.g., webhook). If not in GA, docs must state Console-only.
- Ensure “insufficient volume” guidance text matches design copy and does not confuse customers about split accuracy.

Links
- Confluence PRD: hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd
- Confluence design spec: hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec
- ADR: adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting
- ADR: adr-rollout-policy-evaluation-order-and-precedence
- Runbook: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split
- SLO/alerts: hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts
- Docs PR: redwood-docs PR-922
- Observability: observability-pack PR-184",
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-24 (Paula Mendes): Drafted initial checklist structure. Pulled in audit event requirements from Security and stop-condition needs from SRE. Need owners to confirm default thresholds for GA vs per-tier overrides.",
    "2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Added alerting guidance: route-specific cohort regressions should not page by default; page only for systemic tagging/enforcement/control-plane propagation issues. Request: ensure kill switch is tested in a game day prior to GA.",
    "2025-03-06 (Marcus Lin): Audit events list looks complete. Please ensure actor identity is consistent across Console and API actions (service-to-service calls should still attribute initiating user). Also confirm retention/export constraints are unchanged vs existing audit log product.",
    "2025-03-10 (Dylan Brooks): Console timeline view will surface auto-pause/auto-rollback reasons + link to cohort comparison metrics. Need final copy for low-volume/insufficient-volume states (Design thread pending).",
    "2025-03-14 (Marissa Cole): Updating Beta Exit criteria to require 3 production design partners (not just staging). Added explicit no-go rules (split correctness, rollback reliability, audit coverage).",
    "2025-03-18 (Rafael Mendes): Please add explicit runbook validation step: support should be able to follow runbook to diagnose “bad split” and collect required logs/IDs without engineering involvement. Also note that we saw one beta case where metric evaluation timeouts stalled a rollout; ensure fix is included in GA bundle.",
    "2025-03-22 (Paula Mendes): Incorporated beta learnings: split mismatch incident and metric timeout stall. Added split accuracy tolerance language and clarified that low-volume routes should show guidance vs precise claims."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-9180\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Feature flag + gradual enablement plan for Hosted canary rollouts (Console UI)\",\n  \"status\": \"In Review\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-19\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-24\",\n  \"creator\": \"Connor O'Brien\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Dylan Brooks\",\n  \"project\": \"Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA)\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-28\",\n  \"release\": \"console-2025.04\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"console\",\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"feature-flag\",\n    \"ga-readiness\",\n    \"beta\",\n    \"kill-switch\",\n    \"rbac\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-9123\",\n    \"ENG-9140\",\n    \"ENG-9146\",\n    \"ENG-9152\",\n    \"ENG-9171\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"We need a GA-safe enablement plan for the Hosted canary rollouts workflow (Console wizard + rollout details pages) that supports:\\n- Internal dogfood first (Redwood tenants)\\n- Per-tenant beta enablement (design partner allowlist)\\n- Staged GA rollout (progressive enablement across all tenants)\\n- Clear kill switch behavior that is safe even during an active rollout\\n\\nThis ticket is focused on feature flagging + release mechanics (Console + Console backend + control plane integration points), not the core routing enforcement or orchestrator state machine.\\n\\nContext:\\n- The canary workflow touches Console UI, Console backend orchestration endpoints, policy engine guardrails, routing enforcement, and telemetry.\\n- We need the ability to disable the UI independently from disabling rollout actions, and we need a backstop kill switch that prevents any new canary traffic splits from being applied if we detect risk.\\n\\nGoals\\n1) Separate flags for:\\n   a) UI visibility (wizard entry points, \\u201cCreate rollout\\u201d CTA)\\n   b) API/action gating (create/start/progress/rollback endpoints)\\n   c) Data plane enforcement (traffic split application)\\n2) Per-tenant enablement with an allowlist for beta and an easy path to GA ramp.\\n3) Explicit \\u201ckill switch\\u201d semantics and runbook steps that do not require code deploy to activate.\\n4) Clear monitoring checklist during staged rollout + crisp backout steps.\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Implementing the policy engine itself (tracked in ENG-9146)\\n- Implementing routing primitive / cohorting (tracked in ENG-9123)\\n- Creating dashboards (tracked in ENG-9152 / PRs in observability pack)\\n\\nProposed flag design\\nA) Console UI flag (controls visibility only)\\n- Flag name: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui\\n- Scope: tenant\\n- Default: OFF\\n- Behavior:\\n  - OFF: Hide \\u201cRollouts\\u201d entry point for Hosted routes; do not show wizard; hide rollout create CTA.\\n  - ON: Show UI; still requires API/action flag ON to actually perform mutations.\\n\\nB) Console backend action flag (controls mutation endpoints)\\n- Flag name: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions\\n- Scope: tenant\\n- Default: OFF\\n- Behavior:\\n  - OFF: Return 403 with a structured error (feature_not_enabled) for:\\n    - create rollout\\n    - start rollout\\n    - progress step\\n    - pause/resume\\n    - rollback\\n  - OFF should still allow READ-only endpoints if the tenant already has historical rollout objects (important for support / audit views).\\n\\nC) Control plane / routing enforcement flag (backstop kill switch)\\n- Flag name: platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement\\n- Scope: global + per-tenant override (global OFF is hard stop)\\n- Default: OFF in staging, OFF in prod until beta start date\\n- Behavior:\\n  - If global OFF: do not apply canary split configs in data plane; all traffic goes to baseline. Orchestrator should still be able to transition state to \\u201cPaused (enforcement disabled)\\u201d with a clear reason.\\n  - If global ON but tenant override OFF: same as above for that tenant.\\n  - Notes:\\n    - This flag must be evaluated at the data plane enforcement point (ENG-9123) and should be fail-closed in the direction of safety (i.e., if flag service is unreachable, treat as OFF and route all traffic to baseline).\\n    - We must document expected impact on existing in-flight rollouts (see \\u201cKill switch semantics\\u201d).\\n\\nKill switch semantics (must be documented + tested)\\n- UI kill switch (A) is purely cosmetic: turning it OFF hides UI entry points but does not stop a running rollout.\\n- Actions kill switch (B) prevents new changes from Console, but does not stop enforcement.\\n- Enforcement kill switch (C) is the emergency stop. Turning it OFF should:\\n  1) Immediately stop canary traffic from being served (baseline gets 100%).\\n  2) Preserve the rollout object + timeline; do NOT delete.\\n  3) Orchestrator behavior:\\n     - If an auto-stop is triggered while enforcement is OFF, orchestrator should still be able to pause/rollback states, but those states are mostly bookkeeping. We should present a clear banner in Console: \\u201cTraffic splitting is currently disabled by an operator. Canary traffic is not being served.\\u201d\\n  4) Audit logging:\\n     - Flag flips are not currently in customer audit logs. We should at minimum log an internal audit event (SRE/operator audit log) when (C) changes. (If that\\u2019s out of scope for GA, document it clearly as an internal-only action.)\\n\\nEnablement phases (beta \\u2192 GA)\\nPhase 0: Pre-beta (staging + internal dev)\\n- console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui: ON for Redwood internal tenant(s) in staging\\n- console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions: ON for Redwood internal tenant(s) in staging\\n- platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement: ON in staging only\\n- Goal: validate end-to-end workflow without exposing to external tenants\\n\\nPhase 1: Internal dogfood (prod)\\n- Enable A + B for Redwood internal tenant(s) in prod\\n- Keep enforcement (C) ON globally but set conservative alerting + on-call awareness; confirm kill switch works in prod.\\n- Guardrails:\\n  - Require manual approvals for >5% step for internal dogfood\\n  - Default auto-stop thresholds on (ENG-9158), but tune to avoid alert storms\\n\\nPhase 2: Design partner beta (prod allowlist)\\n- Enable A + B for allowlisted tenants only (per beta tracker)\\n- Keep enforcement (C) ON globally; keep the ability to flip OFF globally if we see systemic issue\\n- Operational requirements:\\n  - Support channel routing defined (on-call + #eng-sre + #support escalations)\\n  - Daily check on cohort dashboards for enabled tenants\\n\\nPhase 3: Limited GA (progressive ramp)\\n- Keep (C) ON globally\\n- Ramp A + B using staged allowlist expansions:\\n  - 5% of eligible tenants \\u2192 25% \\u2192 50% \\u2192 100%\\n- Eligibility definition (initial):\\n  - Hosted routes only\\n  - Tenants with RBAC bundle version including rollout-approver (if approvals enabled)\\n  - Tenants not opted-out of beta features (if we have a general \\u201cbeta\\u201d toggle)\\n\\nPhase 4: Full GA\\n- Set A + B defaults to ON for all tenants\\n- Keep (C) default ON globally, but maintain kill switch operational ownership with SRE/Release on-call.\\n\\nImplementation details\\n- Flag evaluation location:\\n  - A: Console frontend (feature gate routing/UI)\\n  - B: Console backend (authoritative gate on mutations)\\n  - C: Data plane / routing config evaluation (authoritative kill switch)\\n- Flag service: use existing FeatureFlagService (ffsvc) + per-tenant overrides.\\n- Error handling:\\n  - When B is OFF, return consistent error code that Console can render:\\n    - code=FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED, feature=hosted_canary_rollouts, docs_link=\\u2026\\n- Telemetry:\\n  - Emit counter for blocked actions due to feature flag (to detect confusion / misconfig)\\n  - Add logs for enforcement flag OFF events at routing layer to support incident debugging\\n\\nRisks / edge cases\\n- Partial availability: UI ON but actions OFF creates confusion. Mitigation: Console should detect (B) OFF and show a callout \\u201cYour org is not enabled yet. Contact support.\\u201d\\n- A tenant with existing rollouts when flags turn OFF: must preserve read paths; don\\u2019t hard-404.\\n- Flag propagation delays: if (C) flip OFF isn\\u2019t immediate, kill switch isn\\u2019t useful. Need SLO/expectation for propagation (or implement a cached short TTL + push invalidation).\\n- Multi-region behavior: ensure (C) is applied consistently in all regions; if one region still serves canary, we can get inconsistent cohort metrics and customer-visible behavior.\\n\\nDeliverables\\n- Documented enablement plan (this ticket) + runbook snippet for Release/SRE\\n- Flag definitions added to ffsvc registry + Console/backend integration\\n- Console UX behavior for not-enabled states and enforcement-disabled banner\\n- Basic test coverage (unit/integration) for A/B/C gating paths\\n- Checklist for GA day (who flips what, when, and what to monitor)\\n\\nReferences\\n- Design partner enablement/how-to: sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/how-to-enable-hosted-canary-rollouts-for-a-tenant.json\\n- Release checklist draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json\\n- Related: ENG-9123 (data plane enforcement), ENG-9140 (orchestrator), ENG-9158 (auto-stop/rollback)\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Feature flags A/B/C are defined with clear ownership, defaults, scope, and documented semantics\",\n    \"Console frontend is gated by console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui (no dead links / hidden entry points when OFF)\",\n    \"Console backend blocks all rollout mutation actions when console.hosted_canary_rollouts_actions is OFF (read-only still works)\",\n    \"Data plane enforcement respects platform.hosted_canary_rollouts_enforcement as a global kill switch and fails safe to baseline\",\n    \"Console shows clear messaging when UI is ON but actions are OFF (not enabled) and when enforcement is disabled (traffic not being split)\",\n    \"Enablement phases (internal \\u2192 beta allowlist \\u2192 GA ramp) are written with explicit steps and owners\",\n    \"Backout steps are documented and do not require a deploy (flag flip only), including what happens to running rollouts\",\n    \"A minimal monitoring checklist is included (which dashboards, what thresholds, who to page)\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-20 \\u2014 Dylan Brooks: Drafting flag split into UI vs actions vs enforcement. We\\u2019ve been bitten before by \\u201cUI-only\\u201d flags; want backend to be authoritative on mutations. Will propose 3 flags and have data plane treat kill switch as fail-closed-to-baseline.\",\n    \"2025-02-24 \\u2014 Mina Haddad: +1 on enforcement gate at routing layer. If kill switch is only in Console, it\\u2019s useless during an incident. Please ensure the enforcement flag is evaluated per-request or from config refresh with low TTL; don\\u2019t rely on long-lived cached config.\",\n    \"2025-02-25 \\u2014 Sean Gallagher: For prod: we need a single global OFF switch we can flip during an incident without hunting for tenant overrides. Also please document what operators should expect to see in metrics when enforcement is OFF (baseline goes to 100%, canary cohort metrics drop).\",\n    \"2025-03-03 \\u2014 Chloe Martin: Backend gating: I\\u2019ll add FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED structured errors for all mutation endpoints. Read endpoints should stay accessible; we have support cases where customers need to screenshot timelines after we disable features.\",\n    \"2025-03-07 \\u2014 Tessa Morgan: UX request: if UI is enabled but actions are blocked, show a banner explaining \\u201cBeta access required\\u201d and a link to docs/support. Also, for enforcement-disabled, use a strong warning state on the rollout details page so customers don\\u2019t think the rollout is progressing.\",\n    \"2025-03-12 \\u2014 Connor O'Brien: For staged GA ramp, we\\u2019ll start with allowlist expansion (manual) before we flip defaults. Please include a GA-day checklist: which flags flip in what order, and who is on point (Release + SRE).\",\n    \"2025-03-18 \\u2014 Dylan Brooks: Added staged rollout phases + explicit kill switch semantics. Remaining question: do we need internal audit logs for enforcement flag flips? If we can\\u2019t ship customer-visible audit for it, we should at least log to operator audit trail. Marcus/Kevin\\u2014please advise.\",\n    \"2025-03-21 \\u2014 Marcus Lin: Customer-visible audit logging of feature flag flips is out of scope; internal operator audit is recommended. At minimum, log an internal security event with actor + timestamp when the global enforcement kill switch changes. Don\\u2019t block GA on it, but capture in follow-up if not landed.\",\n    \"2025-03-24 \\u2014 Dylan Brooks: Marking In Review. Plan is stable; waiting for final sign-off from SRE (Sean/Rafael) on propagation expectations and from Release (Connor) on ramp steps. Next: align with ENG-9123 implementation on fail-closed behavior.\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9123-hosted-route-traffic-splitting-enforcement.json\",\n    \"sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9140-console-backend-rollout-orchestration-service.json\",\n    \"sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9158-auto-stop-and-rollback-on-slo-breach.json\",\n    \"sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9171-audit-log-events-for-rollout-actions.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/how-to-enable-hosted-canary-rollouts-for-a-tenant.json\",\n    \"sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json\",\n    \"sources/slack/eng-releases/1740638401-beta-enablement-schedule-and-kill-switch.json\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2e4653bb8e1b457b934d7309f140d5f3\"\n}",
