  ],
  "body": "Owner: Connor O\u2019Brien (Release)\nLast reviewed: 2025-04-04\nScope: GA enablement for \u201cHosted canary rollout workflow\u201d (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.\n\nThis checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta \u2192 GA) and should be used as the \u201csingle source of truth\u201d for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.\n\n---\n\n1) Release metadata\n\nRelease name: Hosted Canary Rollouts \u2014 GA\nTarget window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon\u2013Thu)\nPrimary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE\nChange classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging\nBlast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.\n\nApprovers (required for GA flip):\n- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)\n- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)\n- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)\n- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)\n- Release: Connor O\u2019Brien\n\nGo/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement\nAgenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan\n\n---\n\n2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)\n\nCode deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):\n[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)\n[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)\n[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)\n[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)\n[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)\n[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)\n[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)\n\nRBAC + permissions:\n[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)\n[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)\n\nDocs readiness:\n[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)\n[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)\n[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)\n\n---\n\n3) Feature flags / config gates\n\nWe are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be \u201cready,\u201d but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.\n\nA) Console UI gating\nFlag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui\nDefault: OFF\nControls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console\nChecklist:\n[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling\n[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)\n[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA\n\nB) Control plane / orchestrator gating\nFlag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator\nDefault: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call\nControls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths\nChecklist:\n[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured\n[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)\n[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)\n\nC) Dataplane enforcement gating\nFlag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting\nDefault: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist\nControls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes\nChecklist:\n[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active\n[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)\n[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)\n\nKill switches (must exist + verified):\n[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)\n[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane\u2026 allowlist mode)\n[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console\u2026 = OFF)\n\nKill switch ownership + execution:\nPrimary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch\nSecondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag\nTertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan\u2019s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode\n\n---\n\n4) Migrations / schema changes\n\nSchema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)\n\nPre-flight:\n[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema\n[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)\n[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists\n\nExecution:\n[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window\n[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold\n[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)\n\nPost-migration validation:\n[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back\n[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)\n[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)\n\nRollback stance for migrations:\n- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).\n- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.\n\n---\n\n5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch\n\nKey signals for release window (must be pinned in the \u201cGA watch\u201d dashboard):\n\nA) Routing correctness\n[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)\n[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)\n[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly\n\nB) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)\n[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)\n\nC) System health\n[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints\n[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions\n[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)\n[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)\n\nAlert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):\n- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.\n- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.\n\nConfirm templates exist:\n[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)\n[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)\n\n---\n\n6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration\n\nDefault stop conditions (GA defaults) \u2014 confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:\n[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)\n[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute\n[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline\n[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____\n[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)\n\nSafety checks:\n[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback\n[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)\n[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)\n\nRunbook linkage:\n[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)\n\n---\n\n7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification\n\nGuardrails required for GA (PM-1851):\n[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)\n[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions\n[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback\n[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with \u201chow to fix\u201d guidance\n\nRBAC behaviors:\n[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails\n[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps\n[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs\n\nEdge cases to test (quick checklist):\n[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed \u2192 denied, message displayed\n[ ] Attempt step > max jump \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt rollback without permission \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) \u2192 allowed but stop conditions should not thrash\n\n---\n\n8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)\n\nStage 0 \u2014 Internal dogfood (already in progress)\n[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only\n[ ] Run 1\u20132 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes\n[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer\n\nStage 1 \u2014 Design partner cohort (beta) stability check\n[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker\n[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)\n\nStage 2 \u2014 GA soft launch (allowlist)\nTarget: 10\u201320 tenants over first 48 hours\n[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)\n[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch\n[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies\n\nStage 3 \u2014 GA broad availability\n[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist \u2192 available-by-request \u2192 self-serve (per product decision)\n[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to\n\n---\n\n9) Backout / incident plan\n\nPrinciple: Prefer \u201cstop the bleeding\u201d (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.\n\nBackout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):\n\nLevel 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)\n- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF\n- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split\n- Owner: SRE on-call\n- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5\u201310 minutes; error rate normalizes\n\nLevel 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts\n- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR \u201cwrites disabled\u201d mode\n- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)\n- Owner: Control plane on-call\n\nLevel 3: Hide Console UI entry points\n- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF\n- Effect: customers can\u2019t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds\n- Owner: Release / Console on-call\n\nLevel 4: Full service rollback (last resort)\n- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.\n- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval\n\nIncident triggers (examples):\n- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)\n- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region\n- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations\n- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)\n\nComms plan during incident:\n[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)\n[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet\n[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach\n\n---\n\n10) Verification tests (release-day run)\n\nStaging:\n[ ] Run E2E: create \u2192 start \u2192 1% step \u2192 promote \u2192 pause \u2192 rollback \u2192 confirm baseline restored\n[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves\n[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification\n\nProduction (internal tenant only):\n[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route\n[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)\n[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags\n[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)\n\nPost-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):\n[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline\n[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)\n[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly\n\n---\n\n11) Documentation + support readiness\n\nCustomer docs:\n[ ] \u201cHow to run a canary rollout\u201d updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations\n[ ] Troubleshooting section     "GitHub:redwood/pr-28788-rollout-orchestrator-api-create-progress-pause-rollback",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28802-policy-engine-guardrails-for-rollout-actions",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28819-telemetry-tagging-rollout-id-and-cohort",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28877-rollout-activity-log-and-audit-events",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28910-add-rollout-cohort-dashboards-and-alert-templates",
    "GitHub:redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs",
    "GitHub:rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311-rollout-approver-role-and-permissions",
    "Confluence:architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting",
    "Confluence:oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split",

  ],
  "body": "Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release)
Last reviewed: 2025-04-04
Scope: GA enablement for “Hosted canary rollout workflow” (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.

This checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta → GA) and should be used as the “single source of truth” for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.

---

1) Release metadata

Release name: Hosted Canary Rollouts — GA
Target window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon–Thu)
Primary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE
Change classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging
Blast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.

Approvers (required for GA flip):
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)
- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)
- Release: Connor O’Brien

Go/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement
Agenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan

---

2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)

Code deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):
[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)
[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)
[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)
[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)
[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)
[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)
[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)

RBAC + permissions:
[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)
[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)

Docs readiness:
[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)
[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)
[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)

---

3) Feature flags / config gates

We are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be “ready,” but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.

A) Console UI gating
Flag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui
Default: OFF
Controls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console
Checklist:
[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling
[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)
[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA

B) Control plane / orchestrator gating
Flag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator
Default: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call
Controls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths
Checklist:
[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured
[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)
[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)

C) Dataplane enforcement gating
Flag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting
Default: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist
Controls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes
Checklist:
[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active
[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)
[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)

Kill switches (must exist + verified):
[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)
[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane… allowlist mode)
[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console… = OFF)

Kill switch ownership + execution:
Primary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch
Secondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag
Tertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan’s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode

---

4) Migrations / schema changes

Schema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)

Pre-flight:
[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema
[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)
[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists

Execution:
[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window
[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold
[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)

Post-migration validation:
[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back
[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)
[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)

Rollback stance for migrations:
- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).
- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.

---

5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch

Key signals for release window (must be pinned in the “GA watch” dashboard):

A) Routing correctness
[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)
[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)
[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly

B) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)
[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)
[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)
[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)
[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)

C) System health
[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints
[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions
[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)
[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)

Alert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):
- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.
- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.

Confirm templates exist:
[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)
[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)

---

6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration

Default stop conditions (GA defaults) — confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:
[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)
[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute
[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline
[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____
[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)

Safety checks:
[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback
[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)
[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)

Runbook linkage:
[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)

---

7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification

Guardrails required for GA (PM-1851):
[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)
[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions
[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback
[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with “how to fix” guidance

RBAC behaviors:
[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails
[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps
[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs

Edge cases to test (quick checklist):
[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed → denied, message displayed
[ ] Attempt step > max jump → denied
[ ] Attempt rollback without permission → denied
[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) → allowed but stop conditions should not thrash

---

8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)

Stage 0 — Internal dogfood (already in progress)
[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only
[ ] Run 1–2 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes
[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer

Stage 1 — Design partner cohort (beta) stability check
[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker
[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)

Stage 2 — GA soft launch (allowlist)
Target: 10–20 tenants over first 48 hours
[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)
[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch
[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies

Stage 3 — GA broad availability
[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist → available-by-request → self-serve (per product decision)
[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to

---

9) Backout / incident plan

Principle: Prefer “stop the bleeding” (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.

Backout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):

Level 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)
- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF
- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split
- Owner: SRE on-call
- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5–10 minutes; error rate normalizes

Level 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts
- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR “writes disabled” mode
- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)
- Owner: Control plane on-call

Level 3: Hide Console UI entry points
- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF
- Effect: customers can’t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds
- Owner: Release / Console on-call

Level 4: Full service rollback (last resort)
- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.
- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval

Incident triggers (examples):
- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)
- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region
- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations
- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)

Comms plan during incident:
[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)
[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet
[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach

---

10) Verification tests (release-day run)

Staging:
[ ] Run E2E: create → start → 1% step → promote → pause → rollback → confirm baseline restored
[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves
[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification

Production (internal tenant only):
[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route
[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)
[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags
[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)

Post-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):
[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline
[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)
[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly

---

11) Documentation + support readiness

Customer docs:
[ ] “How to run a canary rollout” updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations
[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied

Internal docs:
[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks
[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags

Support enablement:
[ ] Support macro for “How do I do a percentage rollout?” includes current GA availability rules
[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %

---

12) Final sign-offs (fill in during go/no-go)

Product sign-off:
- Marissa Cole: ____ (date/time)
- Paula Mendes: ____ (date/time)

Engineering sign-off:
- Dylan Brooks: ____ (date/time)
- Ethan Park: ____ (date/time)
- Mina Haddad: ____ (date/time)

SRE sign-off:
- Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: ____ (date/time)

Security sign-off:
- Marcus Lin: ____ (date/time)

Release sign-off:
- Connor O’Brien: ____ (date/time)

Notes / open items at time of GA:
- 
- 

Appendix: Known GA limitations (keep aligned with PM-1859)
- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization
- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA
- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only

  "owner": "Simran Kaur",

  "path": "shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/beta-design-partners-tracker-hosted-canary.json",

    "Marissa Cole",
    "Paula Mendes",

    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Dev Patel",
    "Talia Benson"
  ],
  "team": "product-console-rollouts",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "hosted",
    "canary",
    "rollouts",
    "beta",

    "ga-readiness",
    "console",
    "policy-guardrails",
    "telemetry",
    "audit-logs"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "Linear: PM-1843",
    "Linear: PM-1859",
    "Linear: ENG-9123",
    "Linear: ENG-9158",
    "Slack: incidents/1740726110-rollout-split-mismatch-us-east",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-28895-fix-rollout-step-stuck-on-metric-timeout",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-28877-rollout-activity-log-and-audit-events",
    "Jira: SUP-48377"
  ],
  "content": "Last updated: 2025-05-02 (Simran)\n\nPurpose\n- Working tracker for Hosted canary rollout workflow beta design partners.\n- We\u2019re using this to drive: enablement sequencing, feedback capture, GA readiness signal, and comms.\n\nLegend\n- Readiness: \u2705 Ready for GA / \ud83d\udfe1 Conditional / \u274c Not ready\n- Severity: P0 = customer-impacting incident, P1 = blocks rollout workflow, P2 = significant UX/paper cut, P3 = nice-to-have\n- \u201cRoutes involved\u201d refers to Hosted routes in Console (route name) + API path (if applicable)\n\nNotes / reminders\n- Please keep \u201cIssues found\u201d short + link to Jira/Linear/Slack where possible.\n- If a customer requests a feature outside GA scope (quality gates automation, Dedicated parity), capture in \u201cFollow-ups\u201d with owner.\n\nTable (sheet export)\nPartner\tSegment\tPrimary contact (DP)\tEnablement (tenant flag)\tFirst rollout started\tRoutes involved\tBaseline \u2192 Canary\tTraffic schedule used\tGuardrails config used\tSuccess criteria (DP-specific)\tWhat we learned\tIssues found (w/ severity)\tWorkarounds used\tCurrent status\tReadiness for GA\tCan be public reference?\tFollow-ups / owner\nNorthstar Support AI\tAI-native SaaS (support agent)\tSimran Kaur\t2025-03-12\t2025-03-14\tprod-support-chat (/v1/chat/completions)\tllama-3.1-70b-instruct:v2025-02-28 \u2192 v2025-03-10 (same model, new quant profile)\t1%\u21925%\u219225%\u219250%\u2192100% (2h soak)\tMax step=25%; Min soak=60m; Approvals=none; Auto-stop: 5xx>1.0% (5m) OR p95 latency +30% (10m)\t(1) No >0.2% increase in timeouts; (2) p95 latency within +20% at 50%; (3) rollback <2 min; (4) clear UI timeline for exec review\tAuto-stop defaults are a bit \u201ctwitchy\u201d for bursty traffic; metrics compare view was heavily used (p95 + error overlays); they want \u201cexplain why paused\u201d copy to be more explicit\tP1: Rollout auto-paused on brief latency spike (threshold too sensitive) \u2014 SUP-48302;     "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood-docs\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"922\",\n  \"title\": \"Console docs: Hosted canary rollouts GA (concepts, workflow, API, troubleshooting)\",\n  \"author\": \"Wei Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-03-22\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-28\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2025-03-28\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/docs-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Elliot Price\",\n    \"Marissa Cole\",\n    \"Dylan Brooks\",\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Marcus Lin\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"docs\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"hosted\",\n    \"ga\",\n    \"troubleshooting\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"PM-1843\",\n    \"PM-1851\",\n    \"PM-1859\",\n    \"ENG-9140\",\n    \"ENG-9158\",\n    \"ENG-9171\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-48211\",\n    \"SUP-48302\",\n    \"SUP-48377\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"17\",\n  \"additions\": \"914\",\n  \"deletions\": \"203\",\n  \"description\": \"Summary: This PR refreshes and GA-izes our documentation for Hosted canary rollouts in Redwood Console. It consolidates beta-era notes into a single GA narrative, adds a step-by-step UI walkthrough (wizard + rollout details view), documents the relevant API surfaces at a conceptual level (with request/response snippets), and adds troubleshooting guidance aligned with the current orchestrator + policy guardrails + auto-stop behavior. Motivation: Support and design partners repeatedly asked for a single source-of-truth doc that explains (1) what a Hosted canary rollout is, (2) how percentage splits behave, (3) what guardrails/approvals exist, (4) what happens on SLO breach / auto-pause / rollback, and (5) how to debug split mismatches and \\u201cstuck\\u201d steps. This PR is intended to be the doc companion to the Hosted canary workflow GA effort. What\\u2019s included: (1) New docs page: \\u201cHosted canary rollouts (GA)\\u201d covering core concepts (baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time, stop conditions), limitations, and FAQs; (2) Console walkthrough: Create rollout \\u2192 Review & validate \\u2192 Start \\u2192 Progress step \\u2192 Pause/Resume \\u2192 Rollback, with screenshots callouts and copy consistent with the wizard; (3) Guardrails and approvals: explains max step size / minimum soak time / approval gates at a user-facing level, with examples of policy validation errors; (4) Observability: how to interpret baseline vs canary cohort metrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, timeouts) and how auto-stop decisions are made; (5) Troubleshooting: common issues (split mismatch, unexpected auto-pause, rollout cannot progress due to soak/approval) and what to collect for support (rollout_id, route, region, timestamps, activity log events); (6) Security/governance notes: audit log event types and what fields customers can expect to see; (7) Updated docs navigation + redirects from the beta page. Not included: Dedicated/Private rollout parity docs, automated quality-gate setup, and deep policy language reference (those remain follow-ups / internal docs). Screenshots: redacted tenant names + routes; updated to current Console build as of 2025-03-26. Testing: link checker, docs build, and snippet lint pass. Rollout: will publish with Console GA announcement; support macros will link to the troubleshooting section; release notes draft updated separately.\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"docs(console/rollouts): add GA concepts page for Hosted canary rollouts\",\n    \"docs(console/rollouts): add wizard walkthrough + rollout details timeline section\",\n    \"docs(api): document rollout-related fields and query parameters (Hosted only)\",\n    \"docs(troubleshooting): add playbook for auto-pause/rollback + split mismatch\",\n    \"docs(nav): add sidebar entries + redirect beta canary docs to GA page\",\n    \"chore: screenshot refresh + alt text + copy alignment with Console strings\"\n  ],\n  \"changed_files\": [\n    \"site/docs/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollouts-ga.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollouts-walkthrough.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/console/rollouts/rollout-metrics-baseline-vs-canary.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/console/troubleshooting/hosted-rollouts.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/security/audit-logging/rollout-actions.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/api/hosted/rollouts.mdx\",\n    \"site/docs/_redirects\",\n    \"site/sidebars/console.js\",\n    \"site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-wizard-step1.png\",\n    \"site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-wizard-review.png\",\n    \"site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-details-metrics.png\",\n    \"site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-details-timeline.png\",\n    \"site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollback-confirm.png\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"Docs build (gatsby): pass\",\n    \"Markdown/MDX lint: pass\",\n    \"Link checker: pass\",\n    \"Spellcheck (technical dictionary): pass\",\n    \"Screenshot size budget: pass\"\n  ],\n  \"review_conversation\": \"Elliot Price (review): The concepts page looks solid. Two nits: (1) we should be explicit that cohorting is deterministic but not guaranteed to be per end-user unless they provide a stable key; (2) \\u201cauto-rollback\\u201d vs \\u201cauto-pause\\u201d terminology is inconsistent across sections. Also, can we add a short \\u201cWhat data do we log?\\u201d callout in troubleshooting to reduce back-and-forth with support? Wei Chen (author): Updated the cohorting section to call out the default stickiness key (request hash inputs) and added guidance for providing a stable user/session identifier (when available) to get more consistent end-user experience. Also normalized language to \\u201cauto-stop\\u201d with outcomes \\u201cauto-pause\\u201d or \\u201cauto-rollback\\u201d depending on policy. Added a \\u201cCollect this for support\\u201d block with rollout_id, route, region, and timestamps + activity log export. Marissa Cole (review): The UI walkthrough matches the wizard flow, but the warning callouts should match current copy (esp. the rollback confirmation). Also can we mention where approvals show up (timeline vs modal) to set expectations? Wei Chen (author): Synced warning copy and updated screenshots from latest build. Added a note in the Approvals section: approval requests appear as a gated action in the step progression dialog and are recorded in the rollout activity timeline with actor + timestamp. Dylan Brooks (review): API page: please avoid implying these endpoints are public GA for everyone; we have tenant gating during staged rollout. Suggest phrasing: \\u201cavailable for eligible tenants; see enablement\\u201d and link to Console availability note. Also add a small disclaimer about region behavior (split is applied per-request in region after smart routing). Wei Chen (author): Updated wording to \\u201cavailable for eligible tenants\\u201d and added an Availability block. Added a \\u201cHow splits are applied\\u201d note: route selection happens first, then canary split is enforced in the selected region using deterministic cohorting. Sean Gallagher (review): Troubleshooting: add guidance for interpreting short-term latency spikes (warm cache / cold start) and advise minimum soak times before escalating. Also include the default stop-condition signals we page on (5xx, timeouts, p95 regression) without giving exact thresholds (those vary). Wei Chen (author): Added a \\u201cBefore you rollback\\u201d subsection describing warm-up effects and suggesting a minimum observation window aligned with configured soak time. Added a list of common stop-condition signals without embedding exact thresholds. Marcus Lin (review): Audit logging section: please state that audit log event fields vary by plan/retention and include an example event payload, but redact tenant IDs. Also make sure we don\\u2019t claim SIEM export in GA docs unless it\\u2019s actually enabled for Hosted tenants. Wei Chen (author): Added a redacted example event and adjusted wording to \\u201caudit logs can be exported via supported integrations where enabled\\u201d (no blanket SIEM claim). Also added a note about retention depending on plan.\",\n  \"merge_outcome\": \"Merged via squash into main by Elliot Price. Post-merge: publish job scheduled with Console GA announcement bundle.\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Docs: Added GA documentation for Hosted canary rollouts including concepts, Console walkthrough, baseline vs canary metrics interpretation, audit logging overview, and troubleshooting for auto-pause/rollback and split mismatch scenarios.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_conversation\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_3a0a0bdfb2ab4a93aecb7dd9b1773e9a\"\n}",

{
  "repo": "redwood-docs",
  "pr_number": "922",
  "title": "Console docs: Hosted canary rollouts GA (concepts, workflow, API, troubleshooting)",
  "author": "Wei Chen",
  "created_at": "2025-03-22",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-28",
  "merged_at": "2025-03-28",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/docs-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga",
  "reviewers": [
    "Elliot Price",
    "Marissa Cole",
    "Dylan Brooks",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Marcus Lin"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "docs",
    "console",
    "rollouts",
    "hosted",
    "ga",
    "troubleshooting"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "PM-1843",
    "PM-1851",
    "PM-1859",
    "ENG-9140",
    "ENG-9158",
    "ENG-9171"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-48211",
    "SUP-48302",
    "SUP-48377"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "17",
  "additions": "914",
  "deletions": "203",
  "description": "Summary: This PR refreshes and GA-izes our documentation for Hosted canary rollouts in Redwood Console. It consolidates beta-era notes into a single GA narrative, adds a step-by-step UI walkthrough (wizard + rollout details view), documents the relevant API surfaces at a conceptual level (with request/response snippets), and adds troubleshooting guidance aligned with the current orchestrator + policy guardrails + auto-stop behavior. Motivation: Support and design partners repeatedly asked for a single source-of-truth doc that explains (1) what a Hosted canary rollout is, (2) how percentage splits behave, (3) what guardrails/approvals exist, (4) what happens on SLO breach / auto-pause / rollback, and (5) how to debug split mismatches and \u201cstuck\u201d steps. This PR is intended to be the doc companion to the Hosted canary workflow GA effort. What\u2019s included: (1) New docs page: \u201cHosted canary rollouts (GA)\u201d covering core concepts (baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time, stop conditions), limitations, and FAQs; (2) Console walkthrough: Create rollout \u2192 Review & validate \u2192 Start \u2192 Progress step \u2192 Pause/Resume \u2192 Rollback, with screenshots callouts and copy consistent with the wizard; (3) Guardrails and approvals: explains max step size / minimum soak time / approval gates at a user-facing level, with examples of policy validation errors; (4) Observability: how to interpret baseline vs canary cohort metrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, timeouts) and how auto-stop decisions are made; (5) Troubleshooting: common issues (split mismatch, unexpected auto-pause, rollout cannot progress due to soak/approval) and what to collect for support (rollout_id, route, region, timestamps, activity log events); (6) Security/governance notes: audit log event types and what fields customers can expect to see; (7) Updated docs navigation + redirects from the beta page. Not included: Dedicated/Private rollout parity docs, automated quality-gate setup, and deep policy language reference (those remain follow-ups / internal docs). Screenshots: redacted tenant names + routes; updated to current Console build as of 2025-03-26. Testing: link checker, docs build, and snippet lint pass. Rollout: will publish with Console GA announcement; support macros will link to the troubleshooting section; release notes draft updated separately.",
  "commits": [
    "docs(console/rollouts): add GA concepts page for Hosted canary rollouts",
    "docs(console/rollouts): add wizard walkthrough + rollout details timeline section",
    "docs(api): document rollout-related fields and query parameters (Hosted only)",
    "docs(troubleshooting): add playbook for auto-pause/rollback + split mismatch",
    "docs(nav): add sidebar entries + redirect beta canary docs to GA page",
    "chore: screenshot refresh + alt text + copy alignment with Console strings"
  ],
  "changed_files": [
    "site/docs/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollouts-ga.mdx",
    "site/docs/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollouts-walkthrough.mdx",
    "site/docs/console/rollouts/rollout-metrics-baseline-vs-canary.mdx",
    "site/docs/console/troubleshooting/hosted-rollouts.mdx",
    "site/docs/security/audit-logging/rollout-actions.mdx",
    "site/docs/api/hosted/rollouts.mdx",
    "site/docs/_redirects",
    "site/sidebars/console.js",
    "site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-wizard-step1.png",
    "site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-wizard-review.png",
    "site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-details-metrics.png",
    "site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-details-timeline.png",
    "site/static/img/console/rollouts/hosted-canary-rollback-confirm.png"
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "Docs build (gatsby): pass",
    "Markdown/MDX lint: pass",
    "Link checker: pass",
    "Spellcheck (technical dictionary): pass",
    "Screenshot size budget: pass"
  ],
  "review_conversation": "Elliot Price (review): The concepts page looks solid. Two nits: (1) we should be explicit that cohorting is deterministic but not guaranteed to be per end-user unless they provide a stable key; (2) \u201cauto-rollback\u201d vs \u201cauto-pause\u201d terminology is inconsistent across sections. Also, can we add a short \u201cWhat data do we log?\u201d callout in troubleshooting to reduce back-and-forth with support? Wei Chen (author): Updated the cohorting section to call out the default stickiness key (request hash inputs) and added guidance for providing a stable user/session identifier (when available) to get more consistent end-user experience. Also normalized language to \u201cauto-stop\u201d with outcomes \u201cauto-pause\u201d or \u201cauto-rollback\u201d depending on policy. Added a \u201cCollect this for support\u201d block with rollout_id, route, region, and timestamps + activity log export. Marissa Cole (review): The UI walkthrough matches the wizard flow, but the warning callouts should match current copy (esp. the rollback confirmation). Also can we mention where approvals show up (timeline vs modal) to set expectations? Wei Chen (author): Synced warning copy and updated screenshots from latest build. Added a note in the Approvals section: approval requests appear as a gated action in the step progression dialog and are recorded in the rollout activity timeline with actor + timestamp. Dylan Brooks (review): API page: please avoid implying these endpoints are public GA for everyone; we have tenant gating during staged rollout. Suggest phrasing: \u201cavailable for eligible tenants; see enablement\u201d and link to Console availability note. Also add a small disclaimer about region behavior (split is applied per-request in region after smart routing). Wei Chen (author): Updated wording to \u201cavailable for eligible tenants\u201d and added an Availability block. Added a \u201cHow splits are applied\u201d note: route selection happens first, then canary split is enforced in the selected region using deterministic cohorting. Sean Gallagher (review): Troubleshooting: add guidance for interpreting short-term latency spikes (warm cache / cold start) and advise minimum soak times before escalating. Also include the default stop-condition signals we page on (5xx, timeouts, p95 regression) without giving exact thresholds (those vary). Wei Chen (author): Added a \u201cBefore you rollback\u201d subsection describing warm-up effects and suggesting a minimum observation window aligned with configured soak time. Added a list of common stop-condition signals without embedding exact thresholds. Marcus Lin (review): Audit logging section: please state that audit log event fields vary by plan/retention and include an example event payload, but redact tenant IDs. Also make sure we don\u2019t claim SIEM export in GA docs unless it\u2019s actually enabled for Hosted tenants. Wei Chen (author): Added a redacted example event and adjusted wording to \u201caudit logs can be exported via supported integrations where enabled\u201d (no blanket SIEM claim). Also added a note about retention depending on plan.",
  "merge_outcome": "Merged via squash into main by Elliot Price. Post-merge: publish job scheduled with Console GA announcement bundle.",
  "release_notes": "Docs: Added GA documentation for Hosted canary rollouts including concepts, Console walkthrough, baseline vs canary metrics interpretation, audit logging overview, and troubleshooting for auto-pause/rollback and split mismatch scenarios.",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_conversation"
  ],

}

item.aggregated_output:
# Hosted Canary Rollout Workflow — launch readiness

**Decision owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Decision state:** Final v3 — reviewable launch decision  
**Launch date:** Not set  

## Capability and supported scope

The capability is a GA workflow for eligible Hosted API tenants to introduce a new model version or serving configuration on an existing hosted route through deterministic percentage-based canary steps. Customers can create, start, pause, resume, approve, advance, and rollback a rollout; view baseline-versus-canary telemetry and an activity timeline; and rely on policy guardrails, audit events, and SLO-driven auto-stop behavior. [PRD, dsid_63abd3750ce94b12aebc0d25c1f3c45b](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json)

Supported launch scope is hosted routes for eligible, feature-flagged tenants, with per-region split enforcement after route selection. Dedicated/private parity, automated quality gates, time-based scheduling, multi-armed-bandit optimization, and blanket SIEM export are excluded. Auto-pause is the default protection; auto-rollback remains entitlement/policy dependent. [PRD, dsid_63abd3750ce94b12aebc0d25c1f3c45b](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json) [GA docs PR, dsid_3a0a0bdfb2ab4a93aecb7dd9b1773e9a](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs.json)

## Satisfied product gates

| Gate | Evidence-backed status |
|---|---|
| Defined GA workflow and exclusions | Satisfied: PRD specifies workflow, guardrails, permissions, telemetry, auditability, rollback target, and non-goals. |
| Customer need | Satisfied: enterprise and regulated customers ask for approvals, audit logs, and change-control evidence. |
| Beta breadth | Satisfied: six design partners enabled and used rollouts, exceeding the five-partner minimum; four report GA-ready and two conditional. [Tracker, dsid_22985fdc50d14444b0d278a5d93f5e08](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/beta-design-partners-tracker-hosted-canary.json) |
| Documentation implementation | Satisfied for code/content readiness: GA concepts, walkthrough, metrics, audit, and troubleshooting docs merged with passing checks. Publication remains coupled to the announcement. [GA docs PR, dsid_3a0a0bdfb2ab4a93aecb7dd9b1773e9a](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs.json) |
| Safe staged enablement mechanism | Satisfied in design: tenant allowlist, progressive enablement, and kill-switch semantics exist in the delivery plan. [ENG-9180, dsid_2e4653bb8e1b457b934d7309f140d5f3](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9180-feature-flag-and-gradual-enablement-hosted-canary-ui.json) |

## Unresolved delivery items

| Item | Owner | Launch impact |
|---|---|---|
| Close ENG-9180 review and verify kill-switch/operator-audit behavior against active rollouts | Dylan Brooks; consult Marcus Lin and Kevin Osei | Blocks broad availability; required before first GA cohort. |
| Resolve actionable policy-denial messaging and insufficient-volume copy | Jordan Lee / Chloe Martin; design owner Kenji Nakamura | Beta partners repeatedly identified unclear rule/role/action messaging; must be fixed or explicitly accepted for limited launch. [Tracker, dsid_22985fdc50d14444b0d278a5d93f5e08](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/beta-design-partners-tracker-hosted-canary.json) |
| Decide and document GA threshold guidance for bursty and long-context traffic | Paula Mendes / Sean Gallagher / Wei Chen | A prior P1 auto-pause sensitivity issue and conditional partner feedback prevent an unconditional GA claim. |
| Confirm customer notification scope (console-only versus webhook) and document the limitation | Marissa Cole / Elliot Price | Open product decision; not a blocker to a scoped launch if console-only is explicit. [PM-1859, dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-1859-ga-launch-criteria-and-beta-exit-checklist-hosted-canary.json) |

## Final recommendation

**CONDITIONAL-GO for a controlled allowlisted launch only; NO-GO for broad GA.** Product definition, beta evidence, merged documentation, audit/RBAC foundations, staged enablement, and kill-switch design justify proceeding only after the pre-launch criteria below are accepted and evidenced. Broad GA remains blocked until all expansion criteria pass. No date is asserted.

## Accepted launch criteria

### Before the first allowlisted tenant

- Final threshold table is filled and signed by product and SRE, including tier/region guidance, minimum samples/windows, soak time, and bursty/long-context handling.
- GA staging game day passes split correctness, stop evaluation, alert actionability, audit attribution, kill switch, and global rollback-to-baseline enforcement in under two minutes.
- No open P0/P1 exists for split correctness, rollback reliability, cross-tenant RBAC, or audit-trail completeness.
- Security signs audit completeness, actor attribution, RBAC isolation, and retention/export posture.
- Release engineering closes the applicable checklist entries and approves backout sequencing.
- Two support trainings are recorded; macros, launch-week SLA, and escalation channel/on-call ownership are active.
- Named product, platform, console, routing, SRE, security, release, docs, and support approvers record go.

### During limited launch

- Scope remains eligible hosted routes and 10–20 allowlisted tenants; existing routes are unchanged unless a rollout is created and started.
- Observe dashboards for at least one hour after each enablement batch.
- Freeze expansion on any routing-correctness anomaly; back out on rollback failure, cross-tenant access/audit defect, or sustained alert storm.
- Preserve console-visible activity and operator audit history when the kill switch is used.

### Before broad GA

- Limited cohort meets the PM-1859 beta/GA exits with no unresolved qualifying incident or P0/P1.
- Partner-conditional issues are resolved or explicitly documented and accepted: burst/long-context threshold guidance, actionable policy-denial copy, audit-event diff completeness, and split-mismatch troubleshooting.
- Release notes and merged docs are published, not merely ready, and support evidence remains current.

## Operational gates and current evidence

| Gate | State | Evidence / acceptance condition | Owner |

## Hard blockers and no-go triggers

Broad GA is blocked by: (1) unsigned default thresholds; (2) no recorded successful GA staging game day; (3) incomplete release checklist; and (4) outstanding SRE, security, release, support, and final product approvals. Any open P0/P1 involving incorrect split enforcement, inability to rollback, or audit-trail gaps is an explicit no-go. Routing anomaly, rollback failure, cross-tenant audit/RBAC defect, or sustained alert storm during staged enablement requires freezing expansion and invoking the backout plan.
